message.content:
# Bug Found!

The issue is on **line 4**. When a larger element is found, the code assigns `arr[0]` (the first element) instead of `arr[i]` (the current element being compared).

## The Problem

```js
if (max < arr[i]) max = arr[0];  // ❌ Wrong - always assigns first element
```

## The Fix

```js
if (max < arr[i]) max = arr[i];  // ✅ Correct - assigns the current (larger) element
```

## Corrected Function

```js
function maxOf(arr) {
  let max = arr[0];
  for (let i = 1; i < arr.length; i++) {
    if (max < arr[i]) max = arr[i];
  }
  return max;
}
```

## Example

| Input | Expected | Buggy Output |
|-------|----------|--------------|
| `[3, 7, 2, 9, 1]` | `9` | `3` |
| `[5, 0, -2, 5]` | `5` | `5` (works by luck) |

The bug causes `max` to always reset to the first element whenever a larger value is found, so the final result is always `arr[0]`.
